code.originalText: Sixteen-week review: medicines, kidneys, mood, caregiver strain and the plan

text.paragraph: Sixteen-week review after the sick visit. [S]

Sugar Ray Robinson returns sixteen weeks after intake with his care partner, four weeks after the sick visit for nausea, loose stools and a slow pulse on donepezil 10 mg. Since returning to 5 mg in the morning his stomach has settled, the vivid dreams stopped, and he has not been dizzy. Metformin and lisinopril were restarted after two days. He had the dilated eye examination two weeks ago, with no retinopathy. He goes to the day program twice a week and to the foundation gym once. His care partner is sleeping better with the day program and the caregiver class. [S]

Alzheimer's disease with early onset (G30.0). Donepezil 5 mg each morning is tolerated; 10 mg was not. He and his care partner prefer to stay at 5 mg for now rather than retry 10 mg or switch to a rivastigmine patch. Memantine is not indicated at the mild stage. [S]
Continue donepezil 5 mg each morning.
MoCA and CDR in six to twelve months.
Revisit the dose, or a rivastigmine patch, if he declines.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.9). Kidney function back to baseline; no retinopathy. [S]

Hemoglobin A1c in five months; eye examination in one to two years.

Mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (F02.A0). Stable; no behavioral symptoms; safe at home with the day program; care partner strain lower. [S]
Continue the day program and the caregiver class.
GUIDE dementia care program when he has Medicare.
Advance care plan reviewed in six months.
